text:
Support: FYI CustZ (dedicated) reports big p99 spike for /v1/generate in eu-west since ~09:05 UTC. p95 ~220ms, p99 ~2.8s. sample request-id: req-0a1b2c3d. They see high TLS handshake times in traces.

Jamal: Any infra changes around 09:00? rolling deploys, edge cfg?

Maria: We rolled a GSLB weight tweak at 08:58 (lowered eu-west weight for AS-path testing) and lowered global DNS TTL to 30s at 08:55 for an unrelated experiment.

Alex: running quick traceroute from EU test probe -> showing extra cross-region hop:
```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (35.201.10.11), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  1.2 ms
 2  52.19.10.5  8.5 ms
 3  203.0.113.45  75.1 ms  <-- unexpected transit via partner AS
 4  35.201.10.11  78.9 ms
```
Seems we're hairpinned through partner network (adds ~70ms).

Lia: I pulled TLS metrics from edge for CustZ: handshake time histogram shows a secondary mode around 600-900ms since 09:02, with tail to 2.5s. Server-side processing unchanged.

Jamal: Can someone run curl from eu-west probe reproducer with X-Request-ID and TLS timing?

Alex: reproducer: `curl -w "time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_total:%{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Cust-ID: custz" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -o /dev/null`
Sample result: `time_connect:0.080 time_appconnect:0.690 time_total:2.82`

Maria: Given GSLB weight change + low TTL, some clients re-resolved and hit a different POP path via partner. Looks like our partner path has intermittent latency.

Jamal: Immediate mitigation options: 1) revert GSLB weights to previous config (undo experiment) 2) apply per-customer route pin (pin CustZ to eu-west-1 POP) 3) temporarily raise DNS TTL to avoid flapping. Which do we want first?

Support: Customer is paying for reserved capacity and flagged SLA breach. They want a quick mitigation.

Alex: I applied emergency per-customer route pin to eu-west-1 for CustZ at 09:22 UTC (route-pin:eu-west-1). Pushed via edge-control: `edgectl routes pin --cust custz --pop eu-west-1`.

sre-bot: rollback job for GSLB weights queued by Jamal at 09:25 UTC.

Jamal: Rolled back the GSLB weight tweak at 09:26 UTC. Also raised DNS TTL to 300s to minimize churn.

Lia: Post-mitigation metrics (09:30 snapshot): p95 ~140ms, p99 ~610ms. TLS handshake tail still present but greatly reduced. Customer reports noticeable improvement.

Maria: Network team: please open ticket with partner (AS 64500) for transient path via 203.0.113.0/24 that introduced ~70ms hop. Suspect BGP path preference change.

Alex: Attached tcpdump snippet showing repeated TLS retrans and long handshake when hairpinned (trimmed):
```
09:10:12.123 TLS ClientHello (len 512)
09:10:12.734 TCP retrans from client
09:10:13.210 TLS ServerHello (len 256) - time_appconnect ~1.087s
```
Jamal: Root cause hypothesis: low DNS TTL + GSLB weight change caused re-resolution during our partner testing window, some clients got routed via partner path with higher latency and occasional packet loss causing handshake backoff.

Support: Customer accepted mitigation and will monitor. They asked for postmortem and plan to avoid disruptions during experiments.

Maria: Action items: (1) network team to open partner ticket and confirm BGP policy (2) revert experimental GSLB changes to staging only and add canary guardrails (3) add an automated check: if p99 TLS handshake > 500ms for dedicated customers, block GSLB weight experiments.

Jamal: I'll write up a short incident note and link to this thread. Marking incident SEV-3 for now. Will follow-up with network ticket ID and postmortem.

Support: thanks all — keeping the customer updated. :thumbsup:
